analysis: Embedding tying achieved host validation macro HR@10 of 0.4700, improving by 0.0612 over the reported untied HistoryModel result of 0.4088, but remaining 0.0350 below the reported SASRec baseline of 0.5050. Category HR@10 was Movies_and_TV 0.530, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.500, Electronics 0.305, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.545. Electronics had the lowest absolute score; prior category metrics were not supplied, so category-level gains or regressions cannot be determined. The result supports further investigation of shared embeddings, but does not establish the proposed sparse-item mechanism. The trial succeeded and consumed 842.89 allocated GPU-seconds.
code_summary: One independently trained HistoryModel per category shares a single item embedding Parameter between history inputs and candidate scoring. The network retains two causal Transformer blocks, positional embeddings, two-head attention pooling, an MLP context encoder, normalized dot-product scoring, learned scale, and jointly trained item bias. Training uses sampled-softmax cross-entropy with 64 masked uniform negatives, AdamW, seed 42, and one best validation checkpoint per category. The generated predictor imports the tied architecture and strictly loads that category’s checkpoint. Assertions check parameter identity, optimizer deduplication, and score agreement after predictor loading. Four-category routing is preserved without ensembles or separately fitted scorers.
